# Whollar

> Whollar organises household demand for home internet into regional cohorts so
> independent providers bid for the group. Free for households. This file lists
> our resource library for AI crawlers and answer engines.

## Resources
- [How much internet speed do you actually need?](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/internet-speed-how-much-need): activity-by-activity Mbps, what 1 gig is really for, right-sizing.
- [The $487 problem: why Canadians overpay for internet](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/overpaying-internet-canada): the size of the overpayment and why most households never ask.
- [Internet price increase? The promo cliff, explained](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/internet-price-increase-promo-cliff): why introductory rates expire and how to see it coming.
- [Collective switching: what if your street switched at once](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/collective-switching-internet-canada): how pooled demand creates leverage one household lacks.
- [TekSavvy vs Rogers: same cable, half the price](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/teksavvy-vs-rogers-same-cable): how independents resell incumbent lines cheaper.
- [Internet bill breakdown: where your $90 actually goes](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/internet-bill-breakdown-canada): the anatomy of a monthly bill and where the negotiable room sits.
- [How to negotiate your internet bill in Canada](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/negotiate-internet-bill-canada): the leverage that works and where it hits a ceiling.
- [Internet retention offer: what the win-back really says](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/internet-retention-offer-win-back): reading the offer they make when you try to leave.
- [Independent internet providers vs flankers: who's who](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/independent-internet-providers-canada): the ownership map behind the brands on the shelf.
- [Collective switching worked for energy. Internet is next](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/collective-switching-energy-proof): the precedent from group energy switching.
- [How three companies came to own Canadian internet](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/big-three-telecom-canada): concentration and what it does to prices.
- [CRTC internet prices: who actually regulates your bill](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/crtc-internet-prices-canada): what the regulator does and does not set.
- [Cheap internet in Chatham, Ontario: the real map](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/cheap-internet-chatham-ontario): a local market mapped by network type.
- [Best internet in Toronto: how to actually decide](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/best-internet-toronto): why the building outranks the brand.
- [Internet providers in Mississauga: the honest map](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/internet-providers-mississauga): the GTA map with one lane fewer than Toronto.
- [Rural internet in Ontario: every real option explained](https://internet.whollar.ca/blog/rural-internet-ontario): the option ladder from fibre to satellite.
